outcomes: putnami cloud secrets set stores a secret under the config key the application reads, and refuses the requirement name infra/requirements.json lists for it, naming the config key and the command that stores it
nonGoals: One name per secret from declaration to runtime. The requirement name stays lowercase because the infrastructure resource-name grammar is lowercase-only; unifying the two names needs a protocol change
Finding secrets already stored under a requirement name. putnami cloud secrets delete removes one

requirements.text: When the published schema of the project declares no field at the key, and the key is the requirement name of a declared field or object, derived from its config path or from its env binding, putnami cloud secrets set writes nothing, exits with a usage error, and names the declared config key and the putnami cloud secrets set command that stores it. This holds for the <project> <key> form, a dotless key and the --block/--field form.

putnami cloud secrets set stores, with no warning, a key that the published schema declares: a field, an object, a field of an object, or an entry of a map or of an object without declared fields, including in a config block whose path has several segments.

A key that the published schema does not declare and that is no requirement name is stored, and a warning naming the putnami cloud config show --secret-keys command prints after the write succeeds. When the schema read fails with a status other than 404, the key is stored and a warning says it was stored unchecked. A failed write prints no warning.
